hero.intro: A new chapter begins – and it's exciting! In secondary school you develop study skills, discover your own strengths and start thinking about your future.

timetable.heading: Your timetable changes – new subjects ahead
timetable.intro: Moving to secondary school brings new subjects to your timetable. The primary school subject 'Environmental Studies' splits into five separate subjects in Year 7: biology, geography, physics, chemistry and health education.

johdanto.heading: Welcome to secondary school
johdanto.subtitle: First lesson: orientation and survival guide
johdanto.p1: In secondary school you develop study skills, discover your own strengths and start thinking about your future.
johdanto.p2: Everything feels a little new at the start – and that's completely normal.
johdanto.p3: You're not alone – everyone else is in the same situation.

robo_bubble: Psst. I also started from scratch once. Here's the guide that helped. 👇

selviytymisopas.heading: Secondary School Survival Guide
selviytymisopas.subtitle: Four ways to survive everyday secondary school life

robo_tarina.heading: Robo arrives at secondary school
robo_tarina.desc: Get to know Robo and AI – and write a letter to yourself in the future. What do you dream of? What are you afraid of? What do you want to remember?

mission_tervetuloa.heading: Operation Secondary School
mission_tervetuloa.intro: You will do this task in groups. The teacher gives each group an envelope – inside are four checkpoint cards. Solve the checkpoints in order, moving together.
mission_tervetuloa.li1: Open Checkpoint 1 and read the instructions aloud together
mission_tervetuloa.li2: Solve the task – the group decides when it's ready
mission_tervetuloa.li3: Only then open the next card
mission_tervetuloa.li4: At the last checkpoint you prepare a presentation for the whole class

teacher_material.open_link: Open teacher guide and problem cards
teacher_material.desc_tervetuloa: Contains teacher instructions, group passport (print one per group) and laminate checkpoint cards 1–6.
teacher_material.desc_motivaatio: Contains teacher instructions with steps and 6 printable problem cards (one per group). Open in browser and print.
teacher_material.desc_vahvuushuutokauppa: Contains teacher instructions and 4 printable group cards – each with all 15 strengths with checkboxes and point entry fields. Open in browser and print.
teacher_material.desc_tulevaisuus: Contains teacher instructions for the Future task: goals, timing, differentiation tips and debriefing and assessment questions.

challenge.summary_toggle: Summary – what I learned in this lesson
challenge.johdanto_ohje: Write a letter to yourself three years from now: What do you hope to be? What are you afraid of? What is there in you now that you do not want to forget? Keep the letter and read it in 9th grade.
challenge.johdanto_vihje: 💡 Tip: Write honestly — the letter is just for you
challenge.opiskelutaidot_ohje: Create a personal study plan for yourself: choose one subject you want to focus on this week. Write down when you will study, how, and how you will assess your success at the end of the week.
challenge.opiskelutaidot_vihje: 💡 Tip: Small, concrete goals work better than big dreams
challenge.motivaatio_ohje: Keep a motivation diary for a week: write down one thing each day that inspired you to learn — and note whether it was internal (I wanted to) or external (I had to / expected). Reflect at the end of the week: which gives you more energy?
challenge.motivaatio_vihje: 💡 Tip: Even small things count — like that one lesson when time flew by
challenge.vahvuudet_ohje: Create your own strength map: write on paper all the things you think you are good at — even the ones that seem small. Categorize the strengths: social, creative, technical, physical. Which category is your strongest?
challenge.vahvuudet_vihje: 💡 Tip: Ask someone who knows you well to add one strength to the list that you did not notice yourself
challenge.summary_ohje: This lesson you practised imagining the future – the most important skill in a changing world.
challenge.summary_li1: 🚀 I completed the Time Travel to the Future task with Robo
challenge.summary_li2: 💭 I practised imagining what kind of adult I could become
challenge.summary_li3: 💼 I thought about what kind of work I would like to try by 2045
challenge.summary_li4: ⭐ I wrote down one dream and one concrete step
challenge.summary_li5: 🤔 I practised the most important skill: what do I do when I do not know what to do?
challenge.summary_vihje: 💡 Remember: daydreaming is not laziness – it is a skill you can practise!

opiskelutaidot.badge: Survival skill 1 – learn how to learn!
opiskelutaidot.heading: Learn, grow, shine
opiskelutaidot.p1: Everyone learns differently. Some learn by listening, others by doing. A good learner tries different approaches, doesn't give up immediately and asks for help.
opiskelutaidot.p2: Learning is not a gift – it's a skill.
opiskelutaidot.tasks_desc: Four tasks where you practise the most important learning skills.
opiskelutaidot.card4_desc: Try a new way of learning!

pakopeli.heading: Secondary school escape game: learn how to learn!
pakopeli.desc: Can you escape? Solve the tasks and discover your own learning styles by playing.

tiedon_temppeli.heading: 🏛️ Temple of Knowledge
tiedon_temppeli.desc: Can you reach the top of the temple? Speed is everything!

motivaatio.heading: Get inspired again
motivaatio.question: What gets you moving?
motivaatio.subtitle: Motivation can come from two directions – and both work.
motivaatio.inner_heading: I do it because I want to
motivaatio.inner_desc: You get energy from the doing or learning itself.
motivaatio.outer_heading: I do it because I have to or get a reward
motivaatio.outer_desc: Energy comes from outside: a grade, praise or consequences.
motivaatio.q1: Is there a subject that feels easy for you? Why?
motivaatio.q2: Is there a subject you only do because you have to? How does that feel?
motivaatio.q3: What would happen if grades were removed completely?

kadonnut_motivaatio.heading: Lost motivation
kadonnut_motivaatio.desc: Motivation has gone missing – can you find it? Play and discover your own ways to keep going.

motivaatiotori.heading: Motivation Market
motivaatiotori.intro: Each group is given one motivation problem card. First the group comes up with its own solutions, then you go around improving each other's ideas.
motivaatiotori.li1: Read your card's problem aloud to the group
motivaatiotori.li2: Write down all solution ideas on the card (3 min)
motivaatiotori.li3: Move to the next card — add or improve ideas (3 min/round)
motivaatiotori.li4: Return to your own card and choose the best idea
motivaatiotori.li5: Present the problem and winning idea to the class (30 sec)
motivaatiotori.hint: ⏱ Time: 20–25 min · Group size: 3–4 students · Moving

vahvuudet.heading: Know yourself, trust yourself
vahvuudet.p1: Everyone has strengths. When you know yourself, you make better choices.

supervoimat.heading: Superpowers – discover your own strengths!
supervoimat.desc: Play an interactive story and find out what your superpowers are. Make choices and discover yourself!

vahvuushuutokauppa.heading: Strength Auction
vahvuushuutokauppa.intro: Each group is given a budget: 10 points and a list of 15 strengths. The group decides together which 3 strengths it wants to "buy" — and why those ones.
vahvuushuutokauppa.hint: ⏱ Time: 20–25 min · Group size: 3–4 students · Moving

tulevaisuus.heading: Dream, explore, grow
tulevaisuus.p1: You can't know the future in advance — but you can practise imagining it. Dreaming is not laziness. It's a skill needed when the world changes and familiar tools disappear.
tulevaisuus.open_in_tab: 🔗 Open task in its own tab (if the view is cramped)
tulevaisuus.p2: In this lesson you do the Time Travel to the Future task: you travel with Robo to the year 2045, make choices and write about your dreams. At the same time you practise the most important skill: what do I do when I don't know what to do?

teppo.heading: TEPPO – Work-oriented basic education
teppo.subtitle: TEPPO makes working life familiar already in school!
teppo.p1: TEPPO is flexible work-oriented basic education for Years 8–9. Studies alternate between work placement periods at workplaces and teaching at school.
teppo.p2: Applications open in spring January–March – open to all Year 7 and 8 students.
teppo.fact2_desc: 5–7 weeks a year at real workplaces.
teppo.fact3_desc: January–March through Wilma or paper form.
teppo.fact4_desc: Regardless of whether you're aiming for upper secondary or vocational school.
teppo.cta: 💼 Ask your school counsellor about TEPPO – applications open in January!

koulun_jalkeen.heading: After school
koulun_jalkeen.subtitle: Find meaningful activities for your free time.
koulun_jalkeen.p1: School is just part of the day. In your free time you learn things that aren't taught at school — and you might find something that becomes important to you.

structure: Intro: New subjects in lower secondary school – the timetable changes (5 min)
What is student counselling? – infographic and short introduction (5 min)
The lower secondary survival guide – what four skills do you need? (5 min)
Interactive story: Robo arrives at lower secondary school (20–25 min)
Operation Upper School – group task on a station trail (20–25 min)
objectives: You know what new subjects are waiting in 7th grade
You know what student counselling is and who to ask for help
You know what four survival skills you need in lower secondary school
You recognise that feeling nervous in a new situation is normal
You have met Robo and written some thoughts to yourself about the future
summary: You know what new subjects there are in 7th grade
You can name the four skills in the Lower Secondary Survival Guide
You know what student counselling means and who your counsellor is
You have written a letter to yourself – your thoughts saved for the future
You can name at least three adults at school you can ask for help
johdanto.why: The transition from primary to secondary school is one of the most sensitive phases in a student's educational journey: a good start strengthens engagement with school, which predicts both learning outcomes and wellbeing throughout the secondary years. Getting to know the new subjects and student counselling right from the start gives pupils an overview of secondary school — and the four survival skills provide a concrete framework for the whole of secondary school.

structure: Intro: how do you learn best? (5 min)
Escape game: learn how to learn (20 min)
Task stations: memory, reading, schedules, AI (your choice)
Wrap-up: one new technique to try this week (5 min)
objectives: You understand how the brain learns: repetition, sleep, and breaks are part of learning
You try at least one new study technique
You understand that learning is a skill that can be practised — not a gift you are born with
summary: You can explain why cramming the night before a test does not work
You know at least two techniques that help things stick in your memory
You have a plan for how to try a new technique before the next test
opiskelutaidot.why: Research shows that the most effective study techniques — such as self-testing and spaced repetition — are precisely the ones students use least. Learning these techniques now will save you hundreds of hours of work during secondary school, exams, and later further studies.

structure: Intro: when did you last get excited about something? (5 min)
Game: The Lost Motivation (20–25 min)
Discussion: where does motivation come from and where does it go? (10 min)
objectives: You know that motivation is not a fixed trait but a state you can influence
You recognise things that drain or fuel your own enthusiasm
You learn to tell the difference between inner drive and external pressure
summary: You can name three things that affect your own motivation
You know at least one way to get yourself moving on a boring day
You understand the difference: I do it because I want to vs. I do it because I have to
mina-oppijana.why: Motivation research shows that enthusiasm comes from three things: making your own decisions, learning and succeeding, and belonging to a group. When you recognise these, you stop waiting for motivation to 'come back on its own' — and you learn to seek it actively. You will need this skill every time a boring patch hits at school, in a hobby, or later at work.

structure: Intro: what are you good at — even outside school? (5 min)
Activity: Superpowers — find your own strengths (20 min)
Pair discussion: what strength does your friend see in you? (10 min)
objectives: You identify at least three of your own character strengths
You understand that strengths are more than just school subjects
You practise describing yourself positively
summary: You can name your core strengths and give an example of each
You know that strengths can be developed by using them
You have practised saying something good about yourself out loud
omat-vahvuudet.why: Research shows that recognising and using your own strengths is linked to wellbeing and school success. In practice you will need this skill soon: when applying for a work placement, thinking about upper secondary options, and in every situation where you need to say who you are and what you can do.

objectives: You review content from different subjects through a game
You notice which topic areas are strong for you and which need more revision
You experience that recalling information from memory is effective practice
summary: You have reviewed content from several subjects by playing
You know which topics went well and what is worth revising
You have experienced how retrieval practice teaches
tiedon-temppeli.why: A quiz is not just fun — it is proven to be one of the most effective ways to learn. When you have to retrieve an answer from memory, the memory trace strengthens far more than from simply reading. This is called the testing effect.

structure: Intro: what would you like to try sometime? (5 min)
Time travel to the future task: a journey with Robo to 2045, choices and your own dreams (10–15 min)
Debrief: sharing dreams — what came up for many? (10 min)
objectives: You practise imagining different futures
You notice that dreaming and coming up with ideas are skills, not laziness
You learn to act in a situation where there is no ready-made right answer
summary: You have imagined your own future and written down one dream
You can tolerate a situation where there is no right answer
You know that you can shape the future with your own choices — one small step at a time
tulevaisuus.why: Futures researchers talk about futures literacy: the ability to imagine multiple possible futures and act even when you do not know for certain what will happen. Many jobs you will do as an adult do not exist yet — which is why the ability to imagine is just as important a skill as reading or arithmetic.

objectives: You know what TEPPO — the work-oriented basic education programme — is
You know who it is suitable for and how to apply
You can assess whether TEPPO might be the right path for you
summary: You know the basics of TEPPO: who, what, and when to apply
You can explain to a guardian what TEPPO is about
You know who to ask for more information if you are interested
teppo.why: Some people learn best by doing. TEPPO is an official way to complete basic education in which workplace learning and school alternate. It is worth knowing about this already in 7th grade, because applications open in spring — and the decision affects your everyday life.

structure: Intro: what paths are there after lower secondary school? (5 min)
Education system diagram and field-of-study carousel (10 min)
Quiz: which field of study could be your thing? (15 min)
Group task: The world needs you (20–30 min)
objectives: You understand the Finnish education system: upper secondary, vocational training, and other paths
You explore different fields of study and find options that interest you
You realise that there are many routes and no single choice closes all doors
8_koulutus.why: In year 9 you apply to upper secondary education — and a good choice requires knowing what you are choosing from. Research shows that interest in a field predicts staying in studies and thriving better than grades alone. This lesson gives you a year's head start: time to explore, compare, and ask questions before the decision is pressing.
summary: You can sketch the main Finnish education pathways from lower secondary onwards
You have at least 2–3 fields of study that interest you
You know that all kinds of professions are needed to solve the world's problems — including yours

structure: Intro: which strengths do you remember from year 7? (5 min)
Interactive story: Strengths Journey (20 min)
Pair task: Fake Insta — professional identity on social media (20 min)
Discussion task: Influencer as a profession – Dream or nightmare? (10–15 min)
objectives: You deepen your understanding of your own strengths and interests
You connect your strengths to fields of study and professions
You practise presenting your skills to others
You reflect on and justify your own opinion – is social media work real work?
8_vahvuudet.why: Your joint-application choice should be based on what you are good at and what excites you — not on where your friends are going. Knowing your strengths is research-proven to be linked to wellbeing, and in practice you will need this next year: in application motivations, entrance and aptitude tests, and in seeking work experience and summer jobs.
summary: You can name your strengths and connect them to at least one profession or field
You have practised telling others about yourself in an interesting and honest way
You notice that the same strength can lead to many different fields

structure: Intro: what does work experience mean and why do we do it? (5 min)
Work experience pathway: six steps from form to reference letter (15 min)
Activity task: Spin the wheel — random career (20 min)
Discussion task: What is work really? (10 min)
objectives: You know the steps of a work experience period and can find a placement for yourself
You dare to contact an employer
You discover that even a surprising job can teach and interest you
You discuss together: what is work really – and what can't you learn about it at school?
8_tet.why: Work experience is for most students their first personal contact with working life, and experiential learning research shows: doing and experiencing teaches things about working life that cannot be learned from a book. Career theories also highlight the role of chance — many people find their path through a surprising experience. So it's worth trying with an open mind.
summary: You know the work experience process from start to finish: form, finding a placement, the week itself, reference letter
You have practised how to ask for a work placement
You can approach even unfamiliar fields with curiosity

structure: Intro: what's getting in the way of your studying right now? (5 min)
Learning clinic: choose your card and explore the strategies (15 min)
Clinic appointment: try the strategy in practice (15 min)
Learning prescription for the teacher (5 min)
objectives: You identify the bottleneck in your studying: revision, exam preparation, concentration, or stamina
You get research-based strategies for your specific problem
You make a concrete plan for yourself — your own learning prescription
8_klinikka.why: In year 8 the demands increase and grades start to count in the joint application. Learning research shows that practising study skills should be targeted: one student needs memory techniques, another needs time management. The clinic works like a real appointment — the treatment is chosen based on the problem.
summary: You can name what in your studying needs the most attention
You know at least two strategies that suit your particular situation
You have your own learning prescription that you can show your teacher and guardian

structure: Intro: nobody knows the future — so why bother thinking about it? (5 min)
Team task 1: Build the school of tomorrow (45 min or 2 h)
Team task 2: The workplace of the future (45 min or 2 h)
Debrief: presentations and discussion
objectives: You practise imagining and justifying alternative futures
You plan in a group and defend your ideas constructively
You reflect on your own place in a changing working life
8_tulevaisuus.why: A large part of future jobs do not yet exist. Futures studies speak of futures literacy: the ability to imagine several possible futures rather than waiting for one ready-made answer. This skill helps you make choices that hold up even as the world changes.
summary: You have built a group vision of a school or workplace of the future
You can justify your ideas and listen to others' perspectives
You understand that the future is made — it does not just happen

johdanto.heading: This year you find your direction
johdanto.subtitle: You don't know where yet — but you're starting to figure it out.
johdanto.label: This year
johdanto.text: This year you'll explore fields of education and start to get a picture of what interests you — and why. You don't need to know yet. But this year your direction starts to take shape.

koulutus.heading: Finland's education system
koulutus.subtitle: What options do you have after basic education?
koulutus.p1: In Finland you can choose different paths after basic education. Upper secondary school, vocational education and other options offer different ways to learn and grow.
koulutus.p2: There is no single right route.
koulutus.karuselli_desc: Click an image to view it full screen.
koulutus.testi_heading: Which field of education could be your thing?
koulutus.testi_desc: Make choices, explore different fields and find options that could suit you.
koulutus.alaset_heading: CareerSet – can you recognise the fields?
koulutus.alaset_desc: Sort jobs into the right fields. Your best result is saved to the shared scoreboard!
koulutus.maailma_desc: Choose a problem for your group, assemble a dream team from different fields and plan a solution together.

vahvuudet.heading: What can I do – what do I want?
vahvuudet.subtitle: Strengths and interests guide your choices.
vahvuudet.intro2: Two tasks help you find them.
vahvuudet.vahvuusmatka_desc: Set off on a journey to discover your strengths. Make choices and find where you shine.
vahvuudet.fakeinsta_desc: Create a social media profile on paper where all the content is your strengths. Your partner acts as your social media manager and helps you find them.
vahvuudet.haaste_ohje: Create your own strengths map: write down your important strengths, which situations they suit and where you want to develop. Justify each choice with one concrete example from your own life.
vahvuudet.haaste_vihje: 💡 Tip: Also think about hidden strengths — things that come so naturally to you that you don't even notice them

tet.heading: A peek into working life
tet.subtitle: What is work really like?
tet.p1: The work experience placement is a chance to see working life for real. You gain experience, learn new things and discover what interests you – or doesn't.
tet.polku_ohje: This is how work experience unfolds – click a step to see more information:
tet.paneeli1_heading: 1. School gives you the employment contract form
tet.paneeli1_p1: Before the work experience placement, the student receives a blank employment contract form from the counsellor. The form is an official document that must be delivered to the future work experience employer.
tet.paneeli1_vihje: 📋 Keep the form safe and tidy!
tet.paneeli2_heading: 2. Student goes to ask for a work experience place
tet.paneeli2_p1: The student goes with the form to workplaces they are interested in and asks: "Can I come to you for work experience?"
tet.paneeli2_kyll_html: If the answer is yes → move to the next step
tet.paneeli2_ei_html: If the answer is no → try the next workplace
tet.paneeli2_vihje: 💡 Don't be discouraged – most people find a place after a few attempts!
tet.paneeli3_p1: When the employer agrees, they fill in the employment contract form and sign it. The student receives the completed form.
tet.paneeli3_p2: The student brings the form to the counsellor as soon as possible.
tet.paneeli3_vihje: 📄 Document: employment contract form (completed) → delivered to counsellor
tet.paneeli4_heading: 4. Counsellor keeps it – and returns it before WE
tet.paneeli4_p1: The counsellor keeps the contract and checks it. Shortly before work experience week begins, the counsellor gives the contract back to the student.
tet.paneeli4_p2: If needed, the counsellor also provides travel tickets for getting to the workplace.
tet.paneeli4_vihje: 🎫 Remember: ask the counsellor for travel tickets if you need them!
tet.paneeli5_p1: The student goes to the workplace with the employment contract and any travel tickets. Work experience begins!
tet.paneeli5_vihje: 💼 Work diligently, be on time and behave professionally.
tet.paneeli6_p1: After work experience ends, the employer writes the student a work reference. The student delivers the reference to the counsellor.
tet.paneeli6_vihje: 🏅 Work experience is now complete – well done!
tet.pyora_desc: You get a random, unusual profession. You have 3 minutes to prepare – then you convince everyone with complete seriousness why it's perfect for you.

klinikka.heading: 🧑‍💻 Learning-to-learn clinic
klinikka.subtitle: What's getting in the way of studying? Choose a topic and walk through the path.
klinikka.badge: 🧑‍💻 Done independently on your own device
klinikka.kulku_html:
🧭 Flow: choose topic → answer → choose strategy → write learning key
📎 Submit: download learningrecipe.txt → Classroom
💡 Tip: you can go through several topics

tulevaisuus.heading: What if? – future thinking
tulevaisuus.subtitle: The future begins with one question.
tulevaisuus.p1: Most of the jobs you will end up in don't exist yet. Nobody knows exactly what kind of world is waiting — not researchers, not teachers, not even AI.
tulevaisuus.p2: But that doesn't mean the future happens to you without you. In this lesson we imagine, build and think — what could school be, what kind of workplace is waiting for you, and who are you in all of that.
tulevaisuus.task1_desc: What could school be like — if you got to decide?
tulevaisuus.task1_step1_heading: Luck wheel — What if... · Alone · 5–8 min
tulevaisuus.task1_step1_desc: Everyone spins their own question and answers it. Then share with the group.
tulevaisuus.task1_step2_desc: The group builds the school: Where? What? How? Who? Why?
tulevaisuus.task1_step3_desc: The group chooses the submission format: poster (Canva / hand-drawn) or slide presentation — submitted as a screenshot or file via Classroom.
tulevaisuus.submission_desc: The group decides together how to present their school. All options work.
tulevaisuus.canva_desc_html: Open canva.com → choose "Poster" or "Presentation" → add text, images and colours. Download PDF or screenshot to Classroom.
tulevaisuus.handdrawn_desc: Draw the school floor plan or mind map on paper. Take a clear photo with your phone and send to Classroom.
tulevaisuus.slides_desc: Create 3–5 slides: one per question (Where? What? How? Who? Why?). Share the link or submit PDF to Classroom.
tulevaisuus.submission_tip: 💡 The most important thing isn't the appearance — the most important thing is that the school gets a voice and the ideas become visible.
tulevaisuus.stuck_intro: No ideas coming? That's totally fine. Try these in order — one of them will work.
tulevaisuus.stuck_tip1_p: Decide who does what — it makes it easier to get started.
tulevaisuus.stuck_role1_html: Chairperson — makes sure everyone gets a chance to speak
tulevaisuus.stuck_role2_html: Secretary — writes ideas down without judging them
tulevaisuus.stuck_role3_html: Presenter — tells the rest of the class what was invented
tulevaisuus.stuck_tip2_heading: 💬 Tip 2 — Choose one sentence and continue it
tulevaisuus.stuck_tip2_p: Everyone says aloud how they would continue the sentence. The secretary writes it down.
tulevaisuus.stuck_sentence1: "What if school wasn't a building? It could be..."
tulevaisuus.stuck_sentence2: "What annoys us most about school? What if we just removed that?"
tulevaisuus.stuck_sentence3: "What's the best thing about school? How could we make it even better?"
tulevaisuus.stuck_sentence4: "If there were no exams at all, what would we study instead?"
tulevaisuus.stuck_tip3_heading: 🎯 Tip 3 — One question at a time, not all at once
tulevaisuus.stuck_tip3_p_html: First agree on just one thing: Where is your school? Then the next.
tulevaisuus.stuck_tip3_order_html: Order: Where? → What is learned? → How? → Who teaches? → Why does school exist?
tulevaisuus.stuck_tip4_heading: 🆘 Tip 4 — If nothing else works, do this
tulevaisuus.stuck_tip4_p_html: Everyone writes alone on paper three words: what your school would have — and three words what it wouldn't have. The secretary combines the words. That becomes the school.
tulevaisuus.stuck_final_vihje: 💡 Silence doesn't mean there are no ideas — it often means they're waiting for permission to come out.
tulevaisuus.mission1_p: Each group presents their school to the rest of the class.
tulevaisuus.mission1_li1: The presenter says: where the school is and why it exists
tulevaisuus.mission1_li2: The class votes: which idea was most surprising?
tulevaisuus.mission1_li3: Joint debrief: what did every school have in common?
tulevaisuus.task2_step1_heading: Luck wheel: What if… · Alone · 5 min
tulevaisuus.task2_step1_desc: Everyone spins in turn. Think for a moment — then tell the group what you got.
tulevaisuus.task2_step2_desc: As a group, choose one question and build tomorrow's workplace based on it.
tulevaisuus.spinner_phase1_p: Everyone spins in turn. Think for 30 seconds: what kind of company or place would respond to this situation? Tell the group.
tulevaisuus.spinner_hint: Everyone spins in turn — then share with the whole group
spinner_questions: What if you could print meat at home with a 3D printer?
What if robots cleaned all homes?
What if we lived underwater?
What if you could make food from rubbish?
What if the fridge could be connected to the shop and it ordered food itself?
What if robot friends helped lonely people?
What if everyone could automatically speak any language?
What if all cars drove themselves — without a driver?
What if you could fly to work or school by drone?
What if shopping centres were replaced by forests?
What if robot arms or legs could be attached to a person?
What if there were no pollution in the air at all?
tulevaisuus.build_phase_p: As a group, choose one "What if" situation and build tomorrow's workplace based on it. It doesn't have to be perfect — the most important thing is that you can explain what happens there.
tulevaisuus.lego_title: If your school has LEGO bricks
tulevaisuus.lego_p: Build your workplace from bricks — a building, a device, a vehicle or anything else. It doesn't need to look real. The most important thing is that you can explain what happens there and why it exists.
tulevaisuus.nolego_title: If there are no LEGOs — choose one of these
tulevaisuus.draw_desc: Draw on paper what the workplace looks like from above. Mark the spaces: where work is done, where people rest, what the most important machine or thing is.
tulevaisuus.prototype_desc: Use what you can find: cardboard boxes, pens, paper, tape, erasers. Build something concrete that represents your place.
tulevaisuus.sticker_desc: Write on Post-it notes or paper slips: name, what is done there, who works there, what equipment is needed. Arrange the notes on a table or wall.
tulevaisuus.build_tip: 💡 Finally, take a photo or screenshot — submit to Classroom. And be prepared to present to the rest of the class!
tulevaisuus.mission2_p: Each group presents their workplace — go through four points, others listen and vote at the end.
tulevaisuus.mission2_li1: Situation: What "What if" question did you have?
tulevaisuus.mission2_li2: Name & location: What is your workplace and where is it?
tulevaisuus.mission2_li4: Class votes: Which place would you like to work in yourself?
tulevaisuus.haaste_ohje_html: Write an education system manifesto: what three things would you absolutely want to change in the current school, and why? Justify each change with educational research or your own experience. What benefits or drawbacks could the changes have?
tulevaisuus.haaste_vihje: 💡 Tip: The best ideas emerge when you consider both the student's and the teacher's perspective
